review_items.title: 'Installed' proposed as the completion state for P-VM-031 — treat installed packs as accepted?
review_items.detail: The project manager's message says the campaign is 'complete' with 40 packs installed. The acceptance register shows 37 accepted. Accepting the proposal would make 'complete' mean 'installed' in every answer that names the campaign.
evidence: msg_008: 'all 40 battery packs are installed, so the campaign is complete'
Warranty CES-2025-114 starts at operational acceptance

review_items.title: Arvéa Mobility and 'ARVEA MOBILITY SAS' — same supplier across 3 documents, merge?
review_items.detail: The supplier appears as 'Arvéa Mobility' in the business case and the delivery programme, and as 'ARVEA MOBILITY SAS' in the authority's contract register. Same SIREN in both party blocks.

review_items.title: Avenant n°3 → Annex 7 lines BUS-209..216, matched on the asset range printed in the amendment table — accept?
review_items.detail: The amendment states the range 'BUS-209 – BUS-216'. The extractor expanded it to eight asset links and set their replacement date to 2026-12-31 from 1 April 2026 (effective), received 18 April 2026.

review_items.title: BUS-104 (VALMO, 2017) and BUS-104 (2004 series) — merge on fleet number?
review_items.detail: Fleet number 104 was reissued in 2017. The retired 2004 vehicle keeps its own asset_id, VIN and history. Merging would attach 13 years of the old vehicle's failures to the current one.

review_items.title: Minutes: 'tranche 3 expected to be funded' → approval of P-VM-058?
review_items.detail: The Q2 PPI review minutes record the authority's expectation that the Bureau will fund tranche 3 in October. The extractor proposed an APPROVES edge. The approval register has no decision on P-VM-058.
evidence: msg_014: 'I cannot commit the budget before the vote'

review_items.title: €25,000 external workshop proposed into the P-VM-021 forecast?
review_items.detail: Maintenance proposes sending 4 hybrids to an external workshop while lift set C is down. Whether it belongs in the project forecast or the maintenance operating budget is finance's decision; it is not authorised.

review_items.title: SIG-T1-044 linked to P-VM-008 from drawing revision C — add AFFECTS_ASSET?
review_items.detail: Revision C moves the work limit to 4+010, which takes in the SIG-T1-044 foundation. The link comes from the drawing note; no GIS is connected to confirm the geometry.

review_items.title: Unallocated ledger lines at DEP-SRO (€486,210) proposed to P-VM-047 by cost centre — allocate?
review_items.detail: 138 lines with no project code carry cost centre DEP-SRO, where P-VM-047 is delivered. A shared cost centre is not evidence that a line belongs to a project.
evidence: fin.cost_transaction: 138 lines, project_code null, cost_center DEP-SRO

pivot.title: 'Installed' proposed as the completion state for P-VM-031 — treat installed packs as accepted?
pivot.detail: The project manager's message says the campaign is 'complete' with 40 packs installed. The acceptance register shows 37 accepted. Accepting the proposal would make 'complete' mean 'installed' in every answer that names the campaign.
pivot.why_pivot: This item changes what a word means, not what a row says. Accepting it silently would make 'complete' mean 'installed' in every answer about the campaign — and start three warranties early.
evidence: msg_008: 'all 40 battery packs are installed, so the campaign is complete'
Warranty CES-2025-114 starts at operational acceptance

options.label: Create a 'complete' state = accepted
options.consequence: Adds a state; 'complete' then means accepted, never installed.

sanity_checks.question: Which renewal projects need intervention this week, and why?
sanity_checks.verdict_body: The walk is Project -> ScheduleTask (baseline vs current) and Project -> PurchaseOrderLine -> Supplier statements, plus Project -> AccessWindow. It ranks by the agreed rules and never collapses them into one score. Supplier dates read from correspondence stay unconfirmed.

sanity_checks.plan:
MATCH (p:Project)-[:HAS_TASK]->(t:ScheduleTask)
OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[:COMMITS]->(po:PurchaseOrderLine)
OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[:REQUIRES_ACCESS]->(a:AccessWindow)
RETURN p, t, po, a

sanity_checks.question: Who pays for the BUS-204 engine repair?
sanity_checks.verdict_body: Asset -> ResponsibilityAssignment (replacement date) -> Clause 34.4 (as restated by AV2) -> Conditions. The notice and cap conditions resolve; the maintenance-default exclusion does not, so the answer is a review item, not a receivable.

sanity_checks.question: Do we have enough buses for peak service while tranche 2 is late and the T1 closure runs?

properties.rationale: Both carry project_code, the capital project key; a project has one budget line per cost category and version.

story_group.story: Keolis Valmont operates the Réseau Valmo under contract DSP-VM-2021 for Valmont Métropole, which owns the network's assets. The renewal portfolio holds 38 projects (29 funded) across bus and tram fleets, depots, track, power and systems. A project is keyed by project_code (P-VM-nnn); a need that has no project yet is keyed N-VM-nnn and lives in intervention_need. Budget lines are kept per approved version; forecasts are snapshots with remaining committed, uncommitted and separately held contingency. Purchase-order lines are commitments, and the supplier's promised date can lag correspondence. Funding claims move through five states — potential, submitted, accepted, disputed, paid — and are never summed as cash. Assets have a canonical asset_id that survives fleet-number reissue. Responsibility is a dated assignment per asset scope and role taken from the contract and its amendments, never inferred from ownership. An open work order does not mean a vehicle is unavailable; availability comes from availability intervals.

grain.Budget_Lines: one project x cost category x budget version
grain.Responsibilities: one asset scope x responsibility role x effective period
